request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?
escalation_reason: The quick pass answered only part of the question.

reply.reply: At passage, estimates indicated the ACA’s coverage expansion would be substantially offset by new revenues and Medicare savings, but the checked passage-era evidence does not establish its net deficit effect. CBO projected $938 billion in coverage-expansion costs over FY2010–FY2019 (CRS R43246, PDF p. 6). A later February 2011 CBO/JCT baseline projected a $210 billion deficit reduction over FY2012–FY2021; that is a later projection, not the passage-era estimate or an actual outcome (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). The brief: output/briefs/case-20261025-153412-679f.html
reply.reasoning: Available verified findings describe projected costs and offset mechanisms, but do not quantify the net deficit impact at passage. The later baseline deficit-reduction projection is clearly distinguished.
